correctness.rationale: The polar partial isometry gives invariant, reducing input/output support spaces even for nonclosed range; on these B_T is unitarily J tensor |T| and is zero on their orthogonal complement. Because Q(s)=(I-sJ)^-1 has positive coefficients, its leading singular value is strictly increasing for s>0. The spectral theorem gives ordinary norm at sup sigma(|T|); quotient continuous functional calculus gives essential norm at Calkin |T|, including finite-rank cores; spectral-measure endpoint gives norm-attainment iff |T| attains its top spectral value. Nilpotent inversion proves radial pseudospectra, exact small-noise exponent and the tridiagonal Volterra benchmark. Independently generated dense complex finite models yielded 196 inverse-norm comparisons, max error 2.27e-13; those comparisons are not the infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: Pseudospectral and essential-resolvent growth are natural nonnormal-operator invariants. It is structurally meaningful that an arbitrary nonnormal, singular or nonattaining core contributes only its norm/essential norm to the entire resolvent profile, and the result separates norm attainment and stability. Same-orientation adjacent blocks need not have this property, so it is not an arbitrary parameter substitution.

final_claim: For a finite positive-weight path of alternating bounded T and T*, the complete ordinary and Calkin essential inverse-resolvent norms are respectively F_m(|z| ||T||) and F_m(|z| ||T||_essential); nontrivial norm attainment, radial pseudospectral disks and the unweighted 1/[2 sin(pi/(4m+2))] constant follow.
limitations: Finite positive-weight paths with one common core and its adjoint only; no arbitrary operator weights or infinite path.
Essential-norm proof requires infinite-dimensional H and does not claim norm attainment when T does not attain.
